paragraphs.title: God Creates the World and Protects Jerusalem

answers: The earth
The heavens
The spirit of man
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD stretches forth the heavens.
easy.q: What does the LORD stretch forth according to the verse?

answers: The earth
Jerusalem
The nations
easy.explanation: The verse describes the LORD as laying the foundation of the earth.
easy.q: What does the LORD lay the foundation of?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD forms the spirit of man within him.
easy.q: What does the LORD form within man?

answers: Stretching forth the heavens, laying the foundation of the earth, and forming the spirit of man
Building Jerusalem, gathering the nations, and defending Judah
Striking the horses, saving the tents, and causing mourning
medium.explanation: The verse presents the LORD as Creator of heaven and earth and as the One who forms the human spirit.
medium.q: Which three actions show the LORD’s power in this verse?

answers: That man is created without God’s involvement
That God forms the human spirit personally and inwardly
That the spirit exists only outside the human body
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes God’s direct work within each person.
medium.q: What does the phrase “within him” emphasize?

answers: A prophetic message from the LORD
A weapon used in battle
A song of celebration
medium.explanation: Here, “burden” refers to a prophetic message or oracle from the LORD.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “burden” mean in “The burden of the word of the LORD”?

answers: It presents Him as having power over all creation
It shows that He is concerned only with people
It describes Jerusalem as an ordinary city
challenge.explanation: The heavens and earth represent the whole created order, showing the LORD’s universal power.
challenge.q: Why does the mention of the heavens and the earth strengthen the description of the LORD?

answers: Both are described as works of the LORD
Only the human spirit is attributed to the LORD
The verse separates them and does not connect either one with God
challenge.explanation: The LORD is shown as both Creator of the world and Former of the human spirit.
challenge.q: What connection does the verse make between creation and the human spirit?

answers: The Creator of the world and the Former of man
Only the king of Jerusalem
Only the military leader of Judah
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the LORD as sovereign over both the universe and human life.
challenge.q: What overall picture of the LORD does this verse give?

paragraphs.title: Jerusalem at the Center of War and Judah’s Deliverance

answers: A cup of trembling
An altar of peace
A stone for building
easy.explanation: The LORD says that Jerusalem will become a cup of trembling to the surrounding peoples.
easy.q: What will Jerusalem become to all the people round about?

answers: They become stronger
They are smitten with astonishment or blindness
They flee into Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The LORD says that He will smite the horses with astonishment and blindness.
easy.q: What happens to the horses of the nations?

answers: The inhabitants of Jerusalem
All the nations
The horses alone
easy.explanation: The passage says that the LORD will defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whom will the LORD defend in that day?

answers: The LORD confuses and weakens them
Judah joins their army
They stop the siege by their own choice
medium.explanation: The LORD strikes the horses and riders and protects Judah and Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why do the nations suffer when they come against Jerusalem?

answers: The inhabitants of Jerusalem through the LORD of hosts
The nations surrounding Jerusalem
Their decision to leave Judah
medium.explanation: The governors say in their hearts that the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be their strength in the LORD.
medium.q: What gives the governors of Judah strength?

answers: A stone that is easy to carry
A heavy stone that injures those who try to lift it
A stone used to build a house
medium.explanation: Jerusalem is compared to a heavy stone that wounds those who burden themselves with it.
medium.q: What does “a burdensome stone” mean in this passage?

answers: It moves from being surrounded by enemies to standing protected in its own place
It changes from a protected city into an abandoned city
It changes from an unmentioned city into a city ruled by the nations
challenge.explanation: Although Jerusalem is besieged, the LORD protects it and causes it to remain inhabited in its own place.
challenge.q: What change in Jerusalem’s position is described throughout the passage?

challenge.answer: So that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem would not magnify themselves against Judah.
challenge.explanation: The verse gives this reason for saving Judah first.
challenge.q: Why does the LORD save the tents of Judah first?

answers: They become like a hearth of fire and a torch of fire against the surrounding nations
They stop defending Jerusalem
They become weaker than the nations
challenge.explanation: The passage compares the governors of Judah to fire that consumes the people around them.
challenge.q: What is the result of strengthening the governors of Judah?

paragraphs.title: A Spirit of Grace, Piercing, and Mourning

answers: The spirit of grace and supplications
A spirit of war only
Water from heaven
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD will pour out the spirit of grace and supplications.
easy.q: What will the LORD pour upon the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem?

answers: Upon the one whom they pierced
Upon the king of the nations
Upon the horses of battle
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “they shall look upon me whom they have pierced.”

answers: As mourning for an only son or firstborn
As a joyful celebration
As another battle
easy.explanation: The mourning is compared to mourning for an only son and for a firstborn.

answers: The spirit leads the people to look upon the pierced one and mourn
The spirit causes the people to flee from Jerusalem
The spirit prevents the people from showing emotion
medium.explanation: After receiving the spirit of grace and supplications, the people look upon the pierced one and mourn.
medium.q: What is the connection between the spirit of grace and the mourning?

answers: It is like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon
It is smaller than ordinary family mourning
It is unnoticed throughout the land
medium.explanation: The passage compares the mourning in Jerusalem with the great mourning of Hadadrimmon.
medium.q: How great is the mourning in Jerusalem?

answers: Earnest prayers or humble requests
Shouts of war
Words of victory
medium.explanation: Supplications are earnest and humble prayers or requests.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “supplications” mean?

answers: The mourning is deep, personal, and intense
The pierced one was certainly an only child
Only one family participated in the mourning
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes the depth of the grief rather than giving a certain family detail.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to an only son or firstborn communicate?

challenge.answer: The people move from receiving grace and supplications to recognizing the pierced one and mourning deeply.
challenge.explanation: The verses describe grace, recognition, bitterness, and widespread mourning.
challenge.q: What emotional movement takes place in these verses?

answers: The passage describes great mourning in Jerusalem and then names many mourning families
Only one person is said to mourn
The nations conduct the mourning
challenge.explanation: The great mourning in Jerusalem is followed by a description of many families mourning separately.
challenge.q: Why is the mourning presented as public rather than merely private?

answers: Every family apart
All together without distinction
Only the family of David will mourn
easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly says that every family will mourn apart.
easy.q: How will the families of the land mourn?

answers: The family of the house of David
The family of Moses
The house of Aaron alone
easy.explanation: The family of the house of David is named first.
easy.q: Which family is specifically named in the passage?

answers: The men and the wives
Only the elders and children
Only the kings and priests
easy.explanation: The passage says that each family mourns apart, and their wives mourn apart.
easy.q: Who mourns separately within the families?

answers: David, Nathan, Levi, and Shimei
Moses, Aaron, Joshua, and Samuel
Reuben, Simeon, Gad, and Asher
medium.explanation: The passage specifically names the houses of David, Nathan, Levi, and Shimei.
medium.q: Which four families or houses are especially mentioned?

answers: Each family and each group within the family mourns separately
No one mourns at all
The families leave the land
medium.explanation: The repetition highlights the separation of the families and of the men and women.
medium.q: What does the repeated phrase “apart” emphasize?

answers: The other families not individually named
The families that left the land
The families that do not participate in the mourning
medium.explanation: The phrase includes all the remaining families in the land.
medium.q: What does “all the families that remain” mean?

answers: The mourning extends throughout the land
The mourning belongs only to the house of David
The other families are unimportant
challenge.explanation: The final verse includes every family that remains, showing the broad scope of the mourning.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the unnamed families also mourn?

answers: It lists many families and groups mourning separately
It describes only one person without a family
It quickly changes from mourning to celebration
challenge.explanation: The repeated listing of families and separate groups emphasizes the extent and seriousness of the grief.
challenge.q: How does the structure of the passage strengthen the sense of mourning?

challenge.answer: Each family mourns separately, and their wives mourn separately as well.
challenge.explanation: The same pattern is repeated for each of the specifically named families.
challenge.q: What do the families of David, Nathan, Levi, and Shimei have in common in this passage?
